featureRequest:
This is revision 2 of 2 of a larger feature. Build only this revision.

The whole feature, as the person asked for it:
# Regroup top-bar controls (and 5 more)

This request comes from a conversation with the developer about their app.
Anything marked suspected or not checked is a guess: confirm it in the code before building on it.

## What this is about
Tinkerdeck's screen overwhelms novices: about 10 ungrouped top-bar controls, six stacked parts per app and up to five banners all show at once, and the features look added one release at a time. The developer wants a tidy-up, not a redesign: regroup controls, hide parts that are not in use (at start and on demand), remember the layout between sessions, add VS Code-style shortcuts and a command palette. Maintained npm packages should be preferred over hand-built components.

## What to build or fix

### 1. Regroup top-bar controls (confirmed)
The top bar has about 10 ungrouped controls: sidebar toggle, logo, name, global Shell dropdown, Editor, Updates, Refresh, Help, theme picker, light/dark toggle and + App. Group related ones, for example shell, theme, updates and help in one Settings menu. Keep sidebar toggle, name and + App visible. The exact list of what counts as advanced is not settled and is to be decided in the plan. Keep the current structure; the editor stays a separate full view.

Evidence:
- src/App.tsx:300-363

### 2. Hide unused parts at start and on demand (confirmed)
An app view stacks AppHeader, GitBar, TabStrip, terminals, ConsoleNav and GitDrawer, and git has two entry points (GitBar and GitDrawer). Up to five banners (lock, job warning, update, manual-update result, error) can show at once, plus about 8 dialogs. Start with optional parts hidden or collapsed. Suggestions (not verified on screen): show GitBar only when the folder is a git repo and the user opens it, or collapse it to a branch chip; collapse ConsoleNav when there is one console; merge update and manual-update banners into one notification spot while keeping lock, job warning and error visible; lazy-load git parts and dialogs with React.lazy/Suspense. Also make open parts hideable, with a 'Reset layout' action that returns to the calm default view. Reset must hide running consoles, not close them, because closing a running terminal asks for confirmation today.

Evidence:
- src/App.tsx:451-531
- src/App.tsx:365-405
- src/App.tsx:549-676
- src/App.tsx:61
- src/App.tsx:62-65
- src/features/editor/EditorView.tsx:12-14

### 3. Remember layout between sessions (confirmed)
Persist the open/hidden state of the optional parts and restore it on the next start. Today only the sidebar collapsed state (paneCollapsed) is read from saved settings. gitTab, help, update and finder flags are not shown to be saved. Whether every part has a hide control today has not been checked.

Evidence:
- src/App.tsx:62-65
- src/App.tsx:69

### 4. VS Code-style keyboard shortcuts (confirmed)
Add shortcuts modelled on VS Code, for example Ctrl+Shift+P palette, Ctrl+` console, Ctrl+Shift+G git, Ctrl+P or Ctrl+O to open the editor. Only Ctrl+B and F5 exist at app level now. The terminal passes only those through, so every new shortcut must be added to the terminal's pass-through list or the terminal will swallow it. The editor has its own Ctrl+S and Ctrl+N, which must not clash.

Evidence:
- src/App.tsx:120-134
- src/features/terminals/TerminalHost.tsx:75-77
- src/features/editor/EditorView.tsx:28

### 5. Command palette (confirmed)
Add a command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) that lists every action with its shortcut, so hidden controls stay findable. Include a 'Reset layout' action and actions for toggling each optional part.

Evidence:
- src/App.tsx:120-134 (no palette or action registry exists today)

### 6. Use maintained npm packages for components (not checked)
Prefer reliable, free, well-supported packages over hand-built components. Candidates (suggestions, not yet verified): cmdk for the palette, react-hotkeys-hook for shortcuts (replacing the hand-written handler), Radix dropdown-menu and dialog for menus and dialogs, react-resizable-panels for panes, React.lazy for lazy loading. Before committing to any package, the plan must check it works with React 18.3 and the Tauri webview, its license and maintenance, and how it fits the app's themes and CSS. None of these is installed today. React 18, framer-motion, marked, dompurify, CodeMirror and xterm are already used.

Evidence:
- package.json (react ^18.3.1, framer-motion; no cmdk, radix or hotkeys packages)
- src/App.tsx:120-134

## Not part of this
- Redesigning the views or their structure
- Moving the editor into the app view; it stays a separate full view
- Log or terminal output noise (the developer meant UI clutter)

## Not settled yet (do not treat as fact)
- Which controls count as advanced and get hidden, and which the developer uses daily?
- Which banners and git entry points stay visible?
- Do all optional parts already have a hide control? Only the state declarations were read.
- Do the candidate packages work with React 18.3, the Tauri webview and the app's styling?
- The CSS and the real on-screen look were not inspected.

## Requirements agreed in the conversation

The developer and the assistant already agreed these while talking. Build on them; do not ask again what they settle.

- **R1**: Inspect the current Tinkerdeck interface and write a tidy-up plan that, for each screen, panel, dialog, footer element, top-bar control and keyboard shortcut, states where it lives afterwards: the named group it belongs to, whether it is shown by default or hidden until needed (by collapsing into a pane or by lazy loading), how it is hidden again once it is open, whether its open/collapsed/hidden state is remembered between sessions, and where any hidden item and each shortcut is reached from.
  - Done when: The plan names every current screen, panel, dialog, footer element, top-bar control and shortcut and states where each one lives after the tidy-up.
  - Done when: The plan states, for each optional part, how it is hidden again after being opened and whether its open/hidden state is saved between sessions.
  - Done when: A reviewer can trace any current function to exactly one place in the plan.
  - Done when: The plan is checked against the running app, not only against src/App.tsx, before it is agreed, including which parts already load lazily and which are always on screen.
  - Done when: The plan says, for each new UI building block it introduces, whether a maintained npm package is used or it is built in-house, and why.
- **R2**: Keep the current screens, panels, dialogs, the footer and the separate editor view; the tidy-up changes only how controls are grouped, which are shown by default or hidden until needed, how open parts can be hidden again, which state is remembered and which shortcuts exist, without redesigning views or embedding the editor inside the app view.
  - Done when: The plan changes only control grouping, default visibility (collapsing or lazy loading), on-demand hiding, remembered layout and shortcuts; it does not redesign or replace existing screens, panels, dialogs or the footer.
  - Done when: The editor remains a separate view rather than being folded into the app view.
  - Done when: The footer stays visible, including after open parts are hidden.
- **R3**: Group related controls into named groups with a stated purpose, keep Shell and Theme directly reachable instead of moving them behind a dialog, and hide advanced or rarely used controls so a first-time user sees fewer controls, while the primary actions (open an app, run a command, open Git, toggle the sidebar) stay visible without opening any hidden area.
  - Done when: A first-time user can point to where opening an app, running a command, opening Git and toggling the sidebar live without opening a hidden or secondary area.
  - Done when: Shell and Theme can be reached without opening a dialog.
  - Done when: Every hidden control is reachable from one clearly named place, and nothing becomes unreachable.
  - Done when: The plan lists each control and whether it is visible by default or hidden as advanced.
- **R4**: Add VS Code-style keyboard shortcuts while keeping the existing app shortcuts: Ctrl+B toggles the sidebar, F5 refreshes, Ctrl+Shift+P opens a command palette, and a shortcut switches the theme.
  - Done when: Ctrl+B toggles the sidebar, F5 refreshes, Ctrl+Shift+P opens the command palette, and the theme shortcut switches the theme.
  - Done when: The app-level shortcuts still work when focus is inside the app view, including when the terminal is focused.
  - Done when: The plan lists every shortcut and what it does, and the command palette lists the actions it can run together with their shortcuts.
- **R5**: Hide parts the user is not working on instead of keeping them on screen: collapse or lazy-load the git tools and the console until they are used, and lazy-load dialogs and tool panels that are not shown, while keeping the git drawer's existing hidden-until-opened behaviour.
  - Done when: Opening an app that has a git repo and a console does not show the git tools or the console until the user asks for them.
  - Done when: A collapsed or lazy-loaded part is reachable when needed, and nothing becomes unreachable.
  - Done when: The parts that are not shown are loaded when needed rather than up front, so the initial view does not carry them.
  - Done when: The git drawer stays hidden until opened, as it does today.
- **R6**: Keep the footer, and make its toggle behave the same as the sidebar's Ctrl+B toggle so the two stay in step.
  - Done when: Clicking the footer toggle and pressing Ctrl+B produce the same result.
  - Done when: The footer remains visible.
- **R7**: Add a command palette that lists every action with its name and its shortcut, so that any control hidden from the default view can still be found and run by typing its name.
  - Done when: The command palette lists every action the app offers, each with the shortcut that runs it, or a clear note that it has none.
  - Done when: Typing the name of a hidden control in the command palette finds that control and runs it.
  - Done when: The command palette opens with Ctrl+Shift+P even when the terminal or editor is focused.
  - Done when: A query that matches no action shows an empty result.
- **R8**: Any optional part the user has opened (the git drawer, the console, extra panes, dialogs and banners) can be hidden again on demand, so after prolonged use the user can return to a calm default view without restarting the app, and hiding an open console does not close the terminal or lose its output.
  - Done when: Every optional part that can be opened also has a control that hides it again.
  - Done when: After hiding the open optional parts, the screen shows the default minimal view with the primary actions and the footer still visible.
  - Done when: A hidden part can be reopened from the same named place, and via the command palette, as when it was first closed.
  - Done when: Hiding an open console keeps the terminal running and its output available, rather than closing it.
- **R9**: Remember the last layout between sessions: for each optional part, whether it is open, collapsed or hidden is saved when the app closes and restored when it reopens, so the user does not have to rearrange the screen each time.
  - Done when: Reopening the app restores the previous session's open, collapsed or hidden state for the optional parts the plan covers (sidebar, git drawer, console, panes and dialogs).
  - Done when: A part the user hid stays hidden in the next session; a part the user left open reopens open.
  - Done when: On first run, or when no saved layout exists, the app starts in the default minimal view.
  - Done when: A saved layout that can no longer be applied falls back to the default for the affected part instead of failing.
- **R10**: Build the new UI building blocks from reliable, free, safe and well-supported npm packages instead of hand-rolling them: the command palette, shortcut handling, menus, dialogs and resizable or collapsible panes each use an established package where a suitable one exists, and anything built in-house is a stated choice with a reason.
  - Done when: For each building block (command palette, keyboard shortcuts, menus, dialogs, resizable or collapsible panes), the plan names the package used or states that it is built in-house with the reason.
  - Done when: Each chosen package is free to use, openly licensed, actively maintained, and confirmed to work with React 18.3 inside the Tauri webview before the plan commits to it.
  - Done when: The chosen packages do not change what the existing controls do, and every existing shortcut still works as R4 requires.
  - Done when: Where the app already has a suitable library installed (for example framer-motion, CodeMirror, xterm), the plan says whether it is reused before adding another.

Not part of this: Implementing the tidy-up in code before the plan is agreed.; Redesigning screens, views or navigation flow, or embedding the editor inside the app view.; Changing what existing functions do; the plan changes where they live, how they are grouped, whether they show by default, whether they are remembered and which shortcuts reach them.; Moving the Shell or Theme controls behind a dialog.; Backend, data-storage or permission changes.

<!--devteam-requirements:-->

These parts are already built and committed on this branch (use them, do not rebuild them):
- Revision 1: R1 to R5 (commit 73a21f3)

This revision builds exactly these requirements (R6 to R10):
- R6: Keep the footer, and make its toggle behave the same as the sidebar's Ctrl+B toggle so the two stay in step.
- R7: Add a command palette that lists every app action with its name and its shortcut (or a clear note that it has none), so any control hidden from the default view can still be found and run by typing its name, and show an empty result when a query matches no action.
- R8: Any optional part the user has opened (the git drawer, the console, extra panes, dialogs and banners) can be hidden again on demand, so after prolonged use the user can return to the calm default view without restarting the app, and hiding an open console keeps the terminal running with its output available.
- R9: Remember the last layout between sessions: for each optional part the plan names, whether it is open, collapsed or hidden is saved when the app closes and restored when it reopens, so the user does not have to rearrange the screen each time; a first run, or an unreadable saved layout, starts in the default minimal view.
- R10: Build the new UI building blocks from reliable, free, openly licensed, actively maintained npm packages that are confirmed to work with React 18.3 inside the Tauri webview, instead of hand-rolling them: the command palette, shortcut handling, menus, dialogs and resizable or collapsible panes each use an established package where a suitable one exists, house-rule jattac libraries are preferred where they perform the same function, and anything built in-house is a stated choice with a reason.

Verified with npm run lint, the targeted vitest files, the full suite (43 files, 414 tests pass) and npm run build.

findings.description: R9 requires every app to open in the calm default - git tools collapsed, git drawer closed, console hidden. Creating and opening an app via 'Add app' -> save bypasses the calm reset that openApp applies, so a stale git drawer (and possibly expanded git tools) reappears in the new app. Route this new-app app-view transition through the same reset used by openApp (setGitTab(null), setGitToolsOpen(false), select the app's first terminal) instead of calling setView("app") directly.
findings.evidence: handleSave() lands a newly created app in the app view with `if (!exists) setView("app")` (line 279) after only L.selectApp() (line 271); unlike openApp() (lines 233-238) it never does setGitTab(null) or setGitToolsOpen(false). gitTab is also not cleared on any leave-app path, e.g. the palette 'Go to Home' run `() => setView("home")` (line 349) and Sidebar onHome (line 480), so an open git drawer survives; GitDrawer renders whenever gitTab is truthy (line 604). Result: from an app with the git drawer open (or after visiting Home with it open), choosing 'Add app' in the EditPane and saving opens the new app with the previous app's Git drawer already on screen (and, for a repo app, expanded git tools if gitToolsOpen was true).
findings.note: handleSave now routes a newly created app through the calm reset: if (!exists) openApp(saved.id, next) at src/App.tsx:289 instead of setView("app"); openApp (src/App.tsx:238-249) clears gitTab and gitTabKept, sets gitToolsOpen false and selects the app's first terminal. src/App.layout.test.tsx:284-309 opens the previous app's git drawer, creates/saves 'Fresh', and asserts no Git drawer or Consoles panel, collapsed git tools and only the new app's terminal visible; it passes in the 13/13 App.layout.test.tsx run of the 428-test suite.

findings.description: The suite is timing-sensitive/flaky under full parallel load; the build report claims a clean full run. Not certainly caused by this revision, but it should be stabilised before relying on the green result.
findings.evidence: One full `npx vitest run` produced 2 intermittent failures - src/App.features.test.tsx > Consoles > 'deleting an app stops its running consoles first' and src/App.updatecheck.test.tsx > 'shows the update banner when there is a newer version' - while an immediate repeat of the same full suite passed 422/422. The targeted reruns of the affected files also passed.

findings.description: Hiding the git drawer loses the in-progress commit message, so R8's edge case 'Hiding the git drawer does not ... lose an in-progress git message' is not met and is not covered by a test.
findings.evidence: The commit-message draft is React state local to ChangesView (ChangesView.tsx:13 `const [message, setMessage] = useState("")`). App renders GitDrawer only while gitTab is set (App.tsx:604) and its Close calls setGitTab(null) (App.tsx:606), so hiding the drawer unmounts ChangesView and a typed message is gone on reopen. useGit holds only the result message (useGit.ts:49 `GitMessage`), not the draft. No test hides then reopens the drawer with a draft in progress.
findings.note: src/App.tsx now keeps the drawer mounted: gitTabKept state (App.tsx:77-79), openGitTab sets both gitTab and gitTabKept (App.tsx:233-237), and the drawer renders inside <div hidden={gitTab === null}> (App.tsx:613-619) so ChangesView and its local `message` state (ChangesView.tsx:13) are not unmounted when the drawer is closed. src/App.layout.test.tsx:140-156 'R8: hiding the git drawer keeps an in-progress commit message when it is reopened' types 'wip: keep me', clicks 'Close git panel', reopens via /Changes/ and asserts the textarea still has the value. I ran `npx vitest run src/App.layout.test.tsx` and all 10 tests passed, including this one; if the drawer were unmounted the textarea would reset and the test would fail.

findings.description: R7's edge case that hide/show commands for every hideable tool (git tools, git drawer, console) appear in the palette and can hide/reopen the tool is proven only for the console; the git-tools and git-drawer palette commands have no test.
findings.evidence: App.tsx:376-382 adds palette rows 'Show git tools'/'Hide git tools' and 'Close git drawer' (and 'Open console' at 385), but no test queries any of these inside the palette dialog. The only palette hide test is 'Hide console' (App.features.test.tsx:378, App.shortcuts.test.tsx:286). App.shortcuts.test.tsx:215-255 only checks the two 'Git: show changes/history' row counts. R8's 'A hidden tool can be reopened ... via the command palette' is likewise untested for git tools, git drawer and console.
findings.note: src/App.shortcuts.test.tsx:295-345 now drives every hideable tool from inside the palette dialog: 'Show git tools' then 'Hide git tools' (asserts aria-expanded true/false and the Fetch row appears/disappears), 'Git: show changes' then 'Close git drawer' then 'Git: show changes' again (asserts the Git complementary panel opens/closes/reopens), and 'Hide console' then 'Open console' (asserts host data-visible false/true and startTerminal called once, stopTerminal never). Ran npx vitest run src/App.shortcuts.test.tsx src/App.layout.test.tsx src/features/command-palette/CommandPalette.test.tsx -> 28 passed.

findings.description: R9's restart edge cases - a console open at close is not restarted and old output is not restored, and a dialog/banner/branch menu/theme finder/app edit form open at close is not reopened with stale content - have no test; only the sidebar flag is exercised across a restart.
findings.evidence: The only restart test (App.layout.test.tsx:191-202) and the sidebar restart test (App.features.test.tsx:455-472) exercise the sidebar flag with no console or dialog open. No test unmounts App with a running console and asserts startTerminal is not called again or old output is not restored. No test reopens with a dialog, banner, branch menu, theme finder or app edit form open and asserts it is not reopened with stale content.
findings.note: confirmed by the whole Challenge after being built (src/App.layout.test.tsx:230-247 now renders App, opens the app's Console (startTerminal called with console-a1:1), unmounts with the console open, remounts, reopens the app and asserts no host-console-a1:1 testid remains, host-t1 is visible and startTerminal is not called again. src/App.layout.test.tsx:249-282 opens the Switch branch dialog, Find themes dialog, Edit app form, the manual-update banner and the Help dialog, unmounts and remounts, then asserts every one is gone. Both tests pass in the run of App.layout.test.tsx (13/13).)

findings.description: R10's plan-based acceptance - each building block's package or in-house decision, the jattac fallback, licence/maintenance/React 18.3 compatibility and reuse-before-adding - is not proven by any test; only the cmdk adoption and lazy load are.
findings.evidence: The only R10 test (App.test.tsx:392-407) asserts cmdk is pinned and a [cmdk-root] renders lazily. No test asserts the plan (docs/ui-tidy-up-plan.md section 15) records a package or in-house reason for each building block (K1-K5), the jattac overflow-menu unusable-file fallback (K3), or licence/maintenance/React-18.3/Tauri-webview confirmation (acceptance lines 1, 2, 4, 5). The R1 plan tests (App.test.tsx:274, 313) check only generic phrases.
findings.note: confirmed by the whole Challenge after being built (src/App.test.tsx:409-452 slices docs/ui-tidy-up-plan.md at '## 15. Package decisions', requires the 'Licence / maintenance' and 'React 18.3 + Tauri WebView2' columns and the 'Reused without replacement' line, parses one K1-K5 row per building block with non-empty block/decision/licence/react cells and an explicit in-house decision for K2-K5, and asserts K1 is 'cmdk 1.1.1' MIT/actively maintained and K3 records the jattac.libs.web.overflow-menu 0.0.35 missing dist/index.css with its fallback. The test passes in the App.test.tsx run (27/27), and the plan section 15 content it reads exists at docs/ui-tidy-up-plan.md:331-350. tsc --noEmit passes.)

findings.description: R6's edge case that the footer toggle and Ctrl+B agree when the editor is focused is not directly tested.
findings.evidence: The editor-focus test (App.shortcuts.test.tsx:144-171) covers Ctrl+S/N/O/W and Ctrl+Shift+P only. No test opens the editor and presses Ctrl+B or uses the footer toggle there; the app-view test (App.features.test.tsx:443) and TerminalHost.shortcuts.test.tsx:77 cover the terminal path but not the editor.

findings.description: The acceptance that the palette lists every app-level command in the plan's command list is only spot-checked, not asserted exhaustively.
findings.evidence: App.shortcuts.test.tsx:222-255 spot-checks 10 global names and 5 app-only names plus the two Git rows; it never asserts Add app, Start/Stop/Restart selected terminal, Git fetch/pull/push/sync, Show/Hide git tools or Close git drawer are present, so dropping one would not fail a test.

findings.description: The acceptance clause that the editor's own file commands are not listed as palette commands is not asserted by any test.
findings.evidence: The editor test proves Ctrl+S/N/O/W still act while the editor is focused (App.shortcuts.test.tsx:144-171) but never asserts Save/New/Open are absent from the palette, and the R7 listing test (215-255) does not query for them.

findings.description: R8's edge cases 'hiding one tool leaves the rest of the layout as it was' and 'a hidden tool still surfaces its signal' are not directly asserted.
findings.evidence: Reset-layout and console-hide tests keep a running console alive, but no test hides one optional tool (console or git tools) and asserts the other parts and the branch chip/banners are unchanged; GitBar.collapse.test.tsx:42-53 checks the chip only in its collapsed default, not after an app-level hide.

findings.description: The accessibility check's keyboard-only path (run a palette command with the keyboard, visible focus at each step, sensible focus after a tool closes) has no test.
findings.evidence: CommandPalette.test.tsx:36-43 chooses an action with userEvent.click, and no test runs a command with ArrowDown/Enter or asserts focus after the footer toggle, the Hide console control or palette close. The accessibility check requires running a command with the keyboard and visible focus at each step.

findings.description: R9's calm app open (git tools collapsed, git drawer closed) is bypassed when the app view is entered by Add-app save or by clicking a sidebar terminal; a drawer left open in the previous app reappears, and no test covers those entry paths.
findings.evidence: The new-app branch of handleSave ends with setView("app") (App.tsx:288) after only L.selectApp(saved.id) (App.tsx:280); unlike openApp (App.tsx:238-249) it never calls setGitTab(null), setGitTabKept(null) or setGitToolsOpen(false), nor selects the app's first terminal. Sidebar onSelectTerminal also enters the app view without those resets (App.tsx:492-495), and onHome / the palette 'Go to Home' leave gitTab set (App.tsx:489, 358). GitDrawer renders whenever gitTabKept is non-null (App.tsx:613-619), so opening a just-created app, or re-entering via a sidebar terminal after leaving with the drawer open, shows the previous app's git drawer (and expanded git tools) instead of the calm default. App.features.test.tsx:415-439 only exercises the openApp path, so this bypass is untested.

findings.description: Keyboard users lose their place when a tool closes: after closing the palette with Escape focus drops to <body>, and closing the git drawer leaves focus on the hidden Close button. This fails the revision's accessibility requirement that the palette and every hide control 'return focus to a sensible place when a tool closes' (and the keyboard check 'closes the palette with Escape ... with visible focus at each step'). Capture the focused element when the palette/drawer opens and restore it on close (or move focus to a named control such as the palette trigger or the Changes/History control).
findings.evidence: The Escape handler closes the palette with onClose() (line 43) and choose() closes it with onClose() (line 57); the component unmounts without saving or restoring document.activeElement. A jsdom probe that renders the palette exactly as App does (open -> input focused -> Escape -> unmount) leaves document.activeElement as BODY. The same gap exists for the git drawer hide control: App.tsx:615-617 wraps GitDrawer in <div hidden={gitTab === null}> and its onClose is () => setGitTab(null), so the focused Close button is hidden with no focus hand-off. The only .focus() calls in src are open-time focus (CommandPalette.tsx:36, Dialog.tsx:19); there is no focus restore anywhere.
findings.note: Moved to the queue as a feature of its own (q-5f04f6) by telegram:6096790972: it no longer blocks this one.

findings.description: The packaged palette exposes an invalid combobox/listbox: the input is role="combobox" with aria-activedescendant pointing at role="button" items carrying an unsupported aria-selected, and the list is announced as "Suggestions" rather than the intended "Commands". Assistive-technology users cannot reliably hear which command is active or that it is selectable. Pass label="Commands" to Command.List and keep cmdk's option role on the items (the rendered element can still be a <button>), and update the A1 role assertions to match.
findings.evidence: Command.List is given aria-label="Commands" (line 78) but cmdk's List reads its `label` prop (default "Suggestions"), so the rendered listbox is aria-label="Suggestions". Command.Item asChild (lines 80-104) wraps a <button role="button"> (line 90), which overrides cmdk's role="option"; the rendered DOM is <div role="listbox" aria-label="Suggestions"> containing <button role="button" aria-selected=...>. Command.Input's aria-label="Search commands" (line 73) is also overridden by cmdk's aria-labelledby to the hidden "Command palette" label.

findings.description: The plan's P11 'Add app' palette command is not proven; the R7 listing test would still pass if that row were dropped.
findings.evidence: The palette coverage test enumerates the global rows (Toggle sidebar, Refresh everything, Switch light/dark theme, Open command palette, Open editor, Check for updates, Help, Go to Home, Find themes, Reset layout) plus a few app-only rows, but never asserts the plan's P11 'Add app' row that App.tsx:363 pushes when the config is not permanently locked; no other palette test mentions it (grep finds 'Add app' only as a pane in App.layout.test.tsx:294 and App.test.tsx:118).

findings.description: R7 acceptance 5's 'editor file commands are not listed as app commands' half has no negative assertion; only the 'continue to work' half is proven.
findings.evidence: The R4/R7 test proves Ctrl+S, Ctrl+N, Ctrl+O and Ctrl+W still save/create/open while the editor is focused, and App.shortcuts.test.tsx:222-235 lists the app-level rows, but no test asserts that Save/New/Open file are absent from the palette's app-level list.

findings.description: R8 acceptance 4 (after hiding the git tools, git drawer and console, the calm default shows the primary actions and the footer) has no single combined assertion, though each individual hide is tested.
findings.evidence: This test hides the git tools, closes the git drawer and hides the console one at a time and checks each leaves; it does not assert the resulting calm view still shows the primary actions and the footer. App.layout.test.tsx:78 checks the footer only after hiding the git tools, and App.layout.test.tsx:113-138 (Reset layout) asserts the TerminalHost visibility and Show git tools but not the footer or primary actions.

findings.description: R6's edge case 'the footer toggle and Ctrl+B work the same when the terminal or editor has focus' is proven for the app view but not for the editor view.
findings.evidence: The focus test drives the footer toggle and Ctrl+B while an app view is focused; App.test.tsx:454 and App.layout.test.tsx:78 cover Home/app, but no test toggles the sidebar from the footer or with Ctrl+B while the separate editor view is mounted, though the editor view renders the Sidebar and AppFooter (App.tsx:483-497, 641-645).
